verses.sa: कृषिगौरक्ष्यवाणिज्यं वैश्यकर्म स्वभावजम् । परिचर्यात्मकं कर्म शूद्रस्यापि स्वभावजम् ॥
verses.tr: Farming, cattle-keeping, and trade are the natural work of the merchant class. Service to others is the natural work of the worker class.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: The Gita has described the duties of warriors, teachers, and rulers. Now it names the work of merchants and service workers, showing how society holds together.

body.text: Farming, cattle-keeping, and trade are the natural work of the merchant class. Service to others is the natural work of the worker class. The word swabhavajam means born of nature. It tells us that farming, cattle-keeping, trade, and service are not random jobs, but duties that belong to particular people by their very nature. A person devoted to their own work attains perfection. Krishna now explains how that devotion leads to perfection.

verses.sa: स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः । स्वकर्मनिरतः सिद्धिं यथा विन्दति तच्छृणु ॥
verses.tr: A person devoted to their own work attains perfection. Listen as I explain how a person devoted to their own work reaches that perfection.
verses.angle: Sve sve: the phrase that rejects imitation
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Listen for a phrase that tells a person to stay in their own lane. Krishna is about to explain exactly how that works.

body.text: A person devoted to their own work attains perfection. Listen as I explain how a person devoted to their own work reaches that perfection. Listen to the phrase sve sve, in each one's own. It appears twice to insist that a person finds fulfillment only by staying devoted to their own work. Krishna promises to explain how a person reaches that perfection through their own work.

verses.sa: यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदं ततम् । स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः ॥
verses.tr: By worshipping the one from whom all beings arise and by whom this whole world is pervaded, a person attains perfection through their own work.
verses.angle: The one source that pervades all beings and all action
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just answered why work is necessary, and now he answers how it becomes sacred. Listen for the single source that connects every action to the divine.

body.text: By worshipping the one from whom all beings arise and by whom this whole world is pervaded, a person attains perfection through their own work. Krishna names the same source twice: from whom all beings arise, and by whom all this is pervaded. That one being is the origin of life and the ground of all action, so any work done for that being becomes a path to perfection. Krishna then moves from the source of all life to the choice of your own work.

verses.sa: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
verses.tr: One's own duty, though imperfect, is better than another's duty well performed. Doing the work set by one's nature, a person does not incur wrongdoing.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna sharpens his point: the duty born of your own nature is safer than copying someone else's path.

body.text: One's own duty, though imperfect, is better than another's duty well performed. Doing the work set by one's nature, a person does not incur wrongdoing. A single word, svadharmah, one's own duty, does the heaviest lifting here. It beats paradharmah, another's duty, even when that other path is flawless, and it frees you from kilbisam, wrongdoing. Next, Krishna continues.

verses.sa: सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् । सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः ॥
verses.tr: O son of Kunti, one should not abandon one's natural duty, even if it has flaws. All undertakings are clouded by some defect, just as fire is veiled by smoke.
verses.angle: Smoke veils fire, so flaws veil all action
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Before you leave a task because it feels imperfect, listen to how Krishna explains why no action is ever perfect.

body.text: O son of Kunti, one should not abandon one's natural duty, even if it has flaws. All undertakings are clouded by some defect, just as fire is veiled by smoke. Krishna says all undertakings are clouded by some defect, just as fire is veiled by smoke. The smoke does not mean the fire is gone; it means the fire is hidden, and you must still do your natural duty. Next, Krishna continues.

verses.sa: असक्तबुद्धिः सर्वत्र जितात्मा विगतस्पृहः । नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धिं परमां संन्यासेनाधिगच्छति ॥
verses.tr: One whose mind is detached everywhere, who has mastered the self, and who is free from craving attains the highest perfection of non-action through renunciation.
verses.angle: asaktabuddhi, a mind free from attachment
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna describes the inner condition that makes duty possible. Listen for the state of a mind that no longer reaches outward.

body.text: One whose mind is detached everywhere, who has mastered the self, and who is free from craving attains the highest perfection of non-action through renunciation. The verse places three qualities side by side, a mind without attachment, a self that has been conquered, and a heart free from craving. Together they make up the path to the highest perfection of non-action. Krishna now turns to the supreme reality that is reached when this state is fully attained.

verses.sa: सिद्धिं प्राप्तो यथा ब्रह्म तथाप्नोति निबोध मे । समासेनैव कौन्तेय निष्ठा ज्ञानस्य या परा ॥
verses.tr: Listen to me briefly, O Arjuna, as I explain how one who has reached perfection attains the supreme reality, the highest culmination of knowledge.
verses.angle: Para, the supreme point of knowledge
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna asks Arjuna to listen to a brief summary of how a perfected seeker attains Brahman. Listen for the word that marks the highest point of this knowledge.

body.text: Listen to me briefly, O Arjuna, as I explain how one who has reached perfection attains the supreme reality, the highest culmination of knowledge. Listen for Para, supreme. It marks the highest point of knowledge, describing the ultimate reality that a perfected seeker attains. Sanjaya then describes the purified understanding and steady self that lead a seeker to this supreme culmination.

verses.sa: बुद्ध्या विशुद्धया युक्तो धृत्याऽऽत्मानं नियम्य च । शब्दादीन् विषयांस्त्यक्त्वा रागद्वेषौ व्युदस्य च ॥
verses.tr: Endowed with purified understanding, holding the self steady with firm resolve, giving up sense-objects, and casting away attraction and aversion...
verses.angle: Krishna speaks to Arjuna, guiding him back to inner steadiness
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna, guiding him back to inner steadiness after the long discourse. Listen to how he describes the discipline of one who seeks the highest reality.

body.text: Endowed with purified understanding, holding the self steady with firm resolve, giving up sense-objects, and casting away attraction and aversion... Krishna speaks to Arjuna, guiding him back to inner steadiness. He describes one who seeks Brahman: a person with clear understanding steadies the mind, restrains the senses, gives up sense pleasures, and drops attraction and aversion. Krishna continues with the result: dwelling in solitude, eating lightly, and controlling speech, body, and mind, one stays absorbed in meditation, grounded in non-attachment.

verses.sa: विविक्तसेवी लघ्वाशी यतवाक्कायमानसः । ध्यानयोगपरो नित्यं वैराग्यं समुपाश्रितः ॥
verses.tr: Dwelling in solitude, eating lightly, and controlling speech, body, and mind, one stays absorbed in meditation, grounded in non-attachment.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues his description of the purified mind, now naming the daily disciplines that keep it steady. Listen for the three things he controls.

body.text: Dwelling in solitude, eating lightly, and controlling speech, body, and mind, one stays absorbed in meditation, grounded in non-attachment. The verse gives a single compound for three restraints, yatah vak kaya manah, meaning one whose speech, body, and mind are restrained. It shows the inner work is an active mastery of every outward and inward movement. Krishna then lists the final qualities, free from ego and anger, that make a person fit for the supreme reality.

verses.sa: अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम् । विमुच्य निर्ममः शान्तो ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥
verses.tr: Free from ego, force, pride, desire, anger, and possession, one becomes peaceful, without “mine,” and fit for union with the supreme reality.
verses.angle: Six poisons to drop for Brahman
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described the outer discipline of solitude and controlled eating. Now he asks: what must drop from inside to finish the job?

body.text: Free from ego, force, pride, desire, anger, and possession, one becomes peaceful, without “mine,” and fit for union with the supreme reality. Notice the list of six poisons that must be dropped before the mind can become peaceful and fit for the supreme reality. When all six are dropped, the person no longer grieves or desires, and becomes equal toward all beings.

verses.sa: ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति । समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मद्भक्तिं लभते पराम् ॥
verses.tr: One who has become Brahman, serene in mind, grieves not and desires not. Equal toward all beings, that person attains supreme devotion to Me.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now shows the fruit of letting go. Listen to the two things a free mind no longer does.

body.text: One who has become Brahman, serene in mind, grieves not and desires not. Equal toward all beings, that person attains supreme devotion to Me. Notice the word prasannatma, serene-minded. It is the mind that has stopped grieving and stopped craving, and that is the very state that allows supreme devotion to grow. Krishna then tells the way to reach that state through loving knowledge.

verses.sa: भक्त्या मामभिजानाति यावान्यश्चास्मि तत्त्वतः । ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम् ॥
verses.tr: Through devoted love, one truly knows Me as I am. Knowing Me in truth, one enters into Me at once.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has finished describing the calm devotee, and now he points to the heart of bhakti. Listen for the word that names this direct knowing.

body.text: Through devoted love, one truly knows Me as I am. Knowing Me in truth, one enters into Me at once. Listen for the word abhijanati, knows truly. It is not ordinary knowledge, but a deep recognition that reveals exactly how much Krishna is and what he is. Krishna now speaks of the devotee who takes refuge in him, acting in the world yet entering the eternal state.

verses.sa: सर्वकर्माण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रयः । मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम् ॥
verses.tr: A devotee who takes refuge in me, while always doing all actions, attains the eternal, imperishable state through my grace.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna shows Arjuna the final shape of devotion, where acting in the world and surrendering to him become one.

body.text: A devotee who takes refuge in me, while always doing all actions, attains the eternal, imperishable state through my grace. Listen to two words, madvyapashrayah and matprasadat. The first means one who takes refuge in me, and the second means by my grace. The verse says the devotee does all actions, yet attains the eternal state only through my grace. Krishna then tells Arjuna to surrender all actions to him and remain constantly focused on him.

prev.title: Three kinds of understanding, resolve and happiness
